latin: Rectius foret illud Becadmin, quod ponit glosa chaldaica super dictione Bresit, exponere de sapientialibus ideis_quam de trigintaduabus uiis, ut dicunt alii Cabalistae; utrunque tamen est rectum in Cabala.
translation: It would be more correct to interpret that 'Becadmin,' which the Chaldean gloss on the term 'Bresit' sets down, as referring to the sapiential ideas, rather than to the thirty-two paths, as other Cabalists say; both, however, are correct within the Kabbalah.
translation_note: Farmer's apparatus records a minor spelling variant in the 1486 print at this point (farmer1998:27652); the entry follows Farmer's base text. 'Becadmin' and 'Bresit' are left transliterated: per Farmer's note, Pico glosses 'Becadmin' as meaning 'with' or 'through eternal things,' and 'Bresit' ('Bereshit') is the opening word of the Torah, 'in the beginning' (paraphrase; farmer1998:27669). 'sapientialibus ideis' (the sapiential ideas) are, per the same note, the Platonic ideas, for Pico originating at the highest level in Christ or 'Wisdom'; the 'thirty-two paths' are the combination of the twenty-two Hebrew letters and the ten sefirot (paraphrase; farmer1998:27669).
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch20, from Latin at farmer1998:27633
attribution: Pico's own opinion (section 11>, Cabalistic conclusions confirming the Christian religion by his own opinion) (farmer1998:27633).
doctrine: Farmer's note glosses 'Becadmin' as 'with' or 'through eternal things' and 'Bresit' as the opening word of the Torah, 'in the beginning'; it associates 'Bresit' with wisdom, the second sefirah and, for Pico, a symbol of Christ, and it identifies the 'thirty-two paths' as the combination of the twenty-two Hebrew letters with the ten sefirot from which, in this tradition, the Wisdom of God created the world (paraphrase; farmer1998:27669). The thesis thus concerns the eternity of the ideas, or of Christ, or of both, and holds both rival Cabalistic readings of the Chaldean gloss to be correct (farmer1998:27633).
historiography: Wirszubski's Pico della Mirandola's Encounter with Jewish Mysticism numbers the thesis the fifty-eighth Kabbalistic conclusion and quotes its Latin in full (wirszubski1989:9114, 9116); no further discursive argument specific to this thesis is given in the material consulted.
not_established: Wirszubski's own interpretive comment, if any, on this specific thesis beyond quoting its Latin is not established in the material consulted (wirszubski1989:9114).
